sources.documentTitle: Fund Management Licensing | Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) (offline fixture title)
sources.sourceText:
If your company wishes to conduct fund management activities regulated under the Securities and Futures Act 2001 (SFA) , it must apply to be a licensed fund management company (LFMC) that holds a capital markets services (CMS) licence.

If your company solely manages venture capital funds, it may apply to be an LFMC that operates under the simplified venture capital fund manager (VCFM) regime.

Individuals performing key functions in a fund management company, such as portfolio construction and allocation, research and advisory, business development and marketing or client servicing are required to be representatives.

You can find out more about fund management activity and the differences between an LFMC and VCFM here.

When we assess your company to be an LFMC or VCFM, MAS considers factors such as:

• Credibility and substantiveness of the business model and plan, and the associated risks;

• Effectiveness of risk management and compliance controls;

• Fund management track record and expertise of an LFMC applicant's management, parent company and major shareholders;

• Fitness and propriety of the applicant, its shareholders and directors; and

• Ability to meet the relevant minimum financial requirements prescribed under the SFA.

In addition, your company needs to operate from a dedicated and secure office space that is accessible only by your company’s directors and staff.

For more information on the admission criteria and applicable requirements, please refer to the Guidelines on Licensing and Conduct of Business for Fund Management Companies.

VCFMs are subject to a simplified set of admission criteria – please refer to Appendix 4 of the aforementioned guidelines.

If your company is able to operate under an existing class exemption, it does not require a licence. Examples of companies that may be eligible for exemption include those that:

• Manage assets for related corporations or related family members;

• Manage a pool of immovable assets for accredited and institutional investors; or

• Manage a pool of non-capital markets products for accredited and institutional investors.

You can find more information on exemptions under section 99 of the SFA and paragraph 5 of the Second Schedule to the Securities and Futures (Licensing and Conduct of Business) Regulations .

outcomes.question: An LFMC's FYE is 31 December. When are audited annual financial returns and auditor's report generally due?
outcomes.answer:
### Statutory Compliance & Legal Authority

**Whole-question status:** Verified general guidance is available. Evidence is incomplete for one or more material issues.

**General statutory guidance:** Verified for the issues identified below; other issues remain incomplete.
**Individual applicability:** General guidance does not by itself establish eligibility or compliance in an individual case.
**Material evidence gaps:** See the evidence gaps and coverage limitations below.

#### Monetary Authority of Singapore — Financial regulation

**Status:** Evidence verified

**Licensed Fund Management Company** (party in scope: Not established)

**MAS LFMC financial returns and SFA reporting requirements** (party in scope: Company)
- **MAS rule explanation:** MAS’s 29 May 2026 SFA compliance toolkit states that an LFMC files quarterly Forms 1 and 2 within 14 days after each quarter end under Regulation 27 of the FMR. It also lists annual audited Forms 1 to 6 and the audited Profit and Loss Account, Balance Sheet and auditor’s report (including a management letter, if any) within five months after financial year end under section 107 of the SFA and Regulation 27 of the FMR. The toolkit says it is non-exhaustive and excludes obligations outside the SFA and fund-level requirements. Confirm the entity’s LFMC scope, reporting period, and current MAS-Tx instructions before applying these deadlines. A complete reporting calendar also needs the licence and manager regime, regulated activities, fund types and reporting periods, plus checks for event-triggered notifications and duties outside this toolkit. One quarterly financial return does not establish that all MAS duties are discharged. [LICENSED FUND MANAGEMENT COMPANIES](https://www.mas.gov.sg/-/media/mas-media-library/regulation/guidance/cmi/compliance-toolkits-for-fund-management-companies/sfa-compliance-toolkit-lfmcs29-may-2026-clean.pdf)

sources.documentTitle: Fund Management Licensing | Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) (offline fixture title)
sources.sourceText:
If your company wishes to conduct fund management activities regulated under the Securities and Futures Act 2001 (SFA) , it must apply to be a licensed fund management company (LFMC) that holds a capital markets services (CMS) licence.

If your company solely manages venture capital funds, it may apply to be an LFMC that operates under the simplified venture capital fund manager (VCFM) regime.

Individuals performing key functions in a fund management company, such as portfolio construction and allocation, research and advisory, business development and marketing or client servicing are required to be representatives.

You can find out more about fund management activity and the differences between an LFMC and VCFM here.

When we assess your company to be an LFMC or VCFM, MAS considers factors such as:

• Credibility and substantiveness of the business model and plan, and the associated risks;

• Effectiveness of risk management and compliance controls;

• Fund management track record and expertise of an LFMC applicant's management, parent company and major shareholders;

• Fitness and propriety of the applicant, its shareholders and directors; and

• Ability to meet the relevant minimum financial requirements prescribed under the SFA.

In addition, your company needs to operate from a dedicated and secure office space that is accessible only by your company’s directors and staff.

For more information on the admission criteria and applicable requirements, please refer to the Guidelines on Licensing and Conduct of Business for Fund Management Companies.

VCFMs are subject to a simplified set of admission criteria – please refer to Appendix 4 of the aforementioned guidelines.

If your company is able to operate under an existing class exemption, it does not require a licence. Examples of companies that may be eligible for exemption include those that:

• Manage assets for related corporations or related family members;

• Manage a pool of immovable assets for accredited and institutional investors; or

• Manage a pool of non-capital markets products for accredited and institutional investors.

You can find more information on exemptions under section 99 of the SFA and paragraph 5 of the Second Schedule to the Securities and Futures (Licensing and Conduct of Business) Regulations .

This compliance toolkit aims to provide LFMCs with a simple reference on the common applications, forms and submissions pursuant to the SFA that are applicable to LFMCs. However, it is not exhaustive, and LFMCs are expected to be familiar with all legislations and requirements that are applicable to them. For the avoidance of doubt, this toolkit excludes reporting obligations that fall outside the SFA; as well as fund-level requirements (e.g. Code of Collective Investment Scheme). Where an LFMC intends to apply for or holds a CMS licence to carry on business in other SFA regulated activities such as dealing in Capital Markets Products, it should also refer to the compliance toolkit that is relevant to these other types of regulated activities. LF MCs are welcomed to provide suggestions on this toolkit using the Guided Form at Contact Us. Relevant to: | LFMCs

outcomes.question: Our VCFM stopped a regulated activity on 1 June. What does the toolkit say about Form 7 and customer obligations?
outcomes.answer:
### Statutory Compliance & Legal Authority

**Whole-question status:** Verified general guidance is available. Evidence verified for mapped issues; full request coverage unconfirmed.

**General statutory guidance:** Verified for all listed issues.
**Individual applicability:** General guidance does not by itself establish eligibility or compliance in an individual case.
**Material evidence gaps:** None identified within the listed guidance. Full request coverage still requires an independent assessment.

#### Monetary Authority of Singapore — Financial regulation

**Status:** Evidence verified

**VCFM Form 7 cessation and noncommencement notification** (party in scope: Company)
- **MAS rule explanation:** A VCFM must submit Form 7, Notice of Cessation of Business, if it ceases to carry on any or all regulated activities. For cessation, the toolkit says to notify MAS within 14 days after the cessation and accompany Form 7 with an audit certification, in no prescribed format, that the VCFM has fully discharged all customer obligations. A VCFM that has not commenced any or all regulated activities by the end of six months from the CMS licence grant must submit Form 7 immediately after that six-month period ends. The cessation deadline applies to cessation of any or all regulated activities. The non-commencement rule applies when any or all regulated activities have not commenced by the end of six months from the licence grant. Form 7 cessation filing includes the stated audit certification of discharged customer obligations. This is a VCFM notification in the toolkit; it does not say that Form 7 is a prior-approval application. The toolkit does not establish the same process for an LFMC or another CMS licence category. For case-specific application, consider: Confirm the licence holder is a VCFM. Whether the event is cessation or non-commencement, the regulated activity affected, and the cessation date or CMS licence grant date. For cessation, whether the required customer-obligations audit certification is available. Do not calculate the non-commencement date without the CMS licence grant date or convert “immediately” into an invented day count. This bounded rule does not cover other VCFM notifications, winding-up duties or client-specific cessation consequences. [VENTURE CAPITAL FUND MANAGERS](https://www.mas.gov.sg/-/media/mas-media-library/regulation/guidance/cmi/compliance-toolkits-for-fund-management-companies/sfa-compliance-toolkit--vcfms29-may-2026-clean.pdf)

outcomes.question: A VCFM was licensed six months ago but has not commenced one regulated activity. When must it notify MAS?
outcomes.answer:
### Statutory Compliance & Legal Authority

**Whole-question status:** Verified general guidance is available. Evidence verified for mapped issues; full request coverage unconfirmed.

**General statutory guidance:** Verified for all listed issues.
**Individual applicability:** General guidance does not by itself establish eligibility or compliance in an individual case.
**Material evidence gaps:** None identified within the listed guidance. Full request coverage still requires an independent assessment.

#### Monetary Authority of Singapore — Financial regulation

**Status:** Evidence verified

**VCFM Form 7 cessation and noncommencement notification** (party in scope: Company)
- **MAS rule explanation:** A VCFM must submit Form 7, Notice of Cessation of Business, if it ceases to carry on any or all regulated activities. For cessation, the toolkit says to notify MAS within 14 days after the cessation and accompany Form 7 with an audit certification, in no prescribed format, that the VCFM has fully discharged all customer obligations. A VCFM that has not commenced any or all regulated activities by the end of six months from the CMS licence grant must submit Form 7 immediately after that six-month period ends. The cessation deadline applies to cessation of any or all regulated activities. The non-commencement rule applies when any or all regulated activities have not commenced by the end of six months from the licence grant. Form 7 cessation filing includes the stated audit certification of discharged customer obligations. This is a VCFM notification in the toolkit; it does not say that Form 7 is a prior-approval application. The toolkit does not establish the same process for an LFMC or another CMS licence category. For case-specific application, consider: Confirm the licence holder is a VCFM. Whether the event is cessation or non-commencement, the regulated activity affected, and the cessation date or CMS licence grant date. For cessation, whether the required customer-obligations audit certification is available. Do not calculate the non-commencement date without the CMS licence grant date or convert “immediately” into an invented day count. This bounded rule does not cover other VCFM notifications, winding-up duties or client-specific cessation consequences. [VENTURE CAPITAL FUND MANAGERS](https://www.mas.gov.sg/-/media/mas-media-library/regulation/guidance/cmi/compliance-toolkits-for-fund-management-companies/sfa-compliance-toolkit--vcfms29-may-2026-clean.pdf)

outcomes.question: We manage three funds as an LFMC. Does the LFMC SFA toolkit establish all fund-level annual reports and investor filings?
outcomes.answer:
### Statutory Compliance & Legal Authority

**Whole-question status:** Verified general guidance is available. Evidence verified for mapped issues; full request coverage unconfirmed.

**General statutory guidance:** Verified for all listed issues.
**Individual applicability:** General guidance does not by itself establish eligibility or compliance in an individual case.
**Material evidence gaps:** None identified within the listed guidance. Full request coverage still requires an independent assessment.

#### Monetary Authority of Singapore — Financial regulation

**Status:** Evidence verified

**MAS LFMC toolkit scope and fund-level requirements** (party in scope: Company)
- **MAS rule explanation:** The MAS LFMC toolkit is a reference for common SFA approvals, notifications and regulatory submissions applicable to LFMCs. MAS says it is not exhaustive and expressly excludes obligations outside the SFA and fund-level requirements, such as the Code of Collective Investment Schemes. It therefore is not a complete checklist for all duties affecting a managed fund. Identify applicable fund-level requirements and other legislation separately. This scope statement applies to the LFMC toolkit; it does not establish the scope of VCFM or other licence-class toolkits. [LICENSED FUND MANAGEMENT COMPANIES](https://www.mas.gov.sg/-/media/mas-media-library/regulation/guidance/cmi/compliance-toolkits-for-fund-management-companies/sfa-compliance-toolkit-lfmcs29-may-2026-clean.pdf)

**Source:** LICENSED FUND MANAGEMENT COMPANIES (live external)
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports MAS LFMC toolkit scope and fund-level requirements): This Compliance Toolkit aims to provide guidance on: Document: | • Applications for approvals from MAS; • Notifications to be submitted to MAS; and • Regulatory submissions to MAS (e.g. financial returns), which are applicable to LFMCs
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports MAS LFMC toolkit scope and fund-level requirements): This compliance toolkit aims to provide LFMCs with a simple reference on the common applications, forms and submissions pursuant to the SFA that are applicable to LFMCs. However, it is not exhaustive, and LFMCs are expected to be familiar with all legislations and requirements that are applicable to them.
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports MAS LFMC toolkit scope and fund-level requirements): For the avoidance of doubt, this toolkit excludes reporting obligations that fall outside the SFA; as well as fund-level requirements (e.g. Code of Collective Investment Scheme).
- Official source: [LICENSED FUND MANAGEMENT COMPANIES](https://www.mas.gov.sg/-/media/mas-media-library/regulation/guidance/cmi/compliance-toolkits-for-fund-management-companies/sfa-compliance-toolkit-lfmcs29-may-2026-clean.pdf)

sources.documentTitle: Fund Management Licensing | Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) (offline fixture title)
sources.sourceText:
If your company wishes to conduct fund management activities regulated under the Securities and Futures Act 2001 (SFA) , it must apply to be a licensed fund management company (LFMC) that holds a capital markets services (CMS) licence.

If your company solely manages venture capital funds, it may apply to be an LFMC that operates under the simplified venture capital fund manager (VCFM) regime.

Individuals performing key functions in a fund management company, such as portfolio construction and allocation, research and advisory, business development and marketing or client servicing are required to be representatives.

You can find out more about fund management activity and the differences between an LFMC and VCFM here.

When we assess your company to be an LFMC or VCFM, MAS considers factors such as:

• Credibility and substantiveness of the business model and plan, and the associated risks;

• Effectiveness of risk management and compliance controls;

• Fund management track record and expertise of an LFMC applicant's management, parent company and major shareholders;

• Fitness and propriety of the applicant, its shareholders and directors; and

• Ability to meet the relevant minimum financial requirements prescribed under the SFA.

In addition, your company needs to operate from a dedicated and secure office space that is accessible only by your company’s directors and staff.

For more information on the admission criteria and applicable requirements, please refer to the Guidelines on Licensing and Conduct of Business for Fund Management Companies.

VCFMs are subject to a simplified set of admission criteria – please refer to Appendix 4 of the aforementioned guidelines.

If your company is able to operate under an existing class exemption, it does not require a licence. Examples of companies that may be eligible for exemption include those that:

• Manage assets for related corporations or related family members;

• Manage a pool of immovable assets for accredited and institutional investors; or

• Manage a pool of non-capital markets products for accredited and institutional investors.

You can find more information on exemptions under section 99 of the SFA and paragraph 5 of the Second Schedule to the Securities and Futures (Licensing and Conduct of Business) Regulations .

sources.documentTitle: Fund Management Licensing | Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) (offline fixture title)
sources.sourceText:
If your company wishes to conduct fund management activities regulated under the Securities and Futures Act 2001 (SFA) , it must apply to be a licensed fund management company (LFMC) that holds a capital markets services (CMS) licence.

If your company solely manages venture capital funds, it may apply to be an LFMC that operates under the simplified venture capital fund manager (VCFM) regime.

Individuals performing key functions in a fund management company, such as portfolio construction and allocation, research and advisory, business development and marketing or client servicing are required to be representatives.

You can find out more about fund management activity and the differences between an LFMC and VCFM here.

When we assess your company to be an LFMC or VCFM, MAS considers factors such as:

• Credibility and substantiveness of the business model and plan, and the associated risks;

• Effectiveness of risk management and compliance controls;

• Fund management track record and expertise of an LFMC applicant's management, parent company and major shareholders;

• Fitness and propriety of the applicant, its shareholders and directors; and

• Ability to meet the relevant minimum financial requirements prescribed under the SFA.

In addition, your company needs to operate from a dedicated and secure office space that is accessible only by your company’s directors and staff.

For more information on the admission criteria and applicable requirements, please refer to the Guidelines on Licensing and Conduct of Business for Fund Management Companies.

VCFMs are subject to a simplified set of admission criteria – please refer to Appendix 4 of the aforementioned guidelines.

If your company is able to operate under an existing class exemption, it does not require a licence. Examples of companies that may be eligible for exemption include those that:

• Manage assets for related corporations or related family members;

• Manage a pool of immovable assets for accredited and institutional investors; or

• Manage a pool of non-capital markets products for accredited and institutional investors.

You can find more information on exemptions under section 99 of the SFA and paragraph 5 of the Second Schedule to the Securities and Futures (Licensing and Conduct of Business) Regulations .
